topIssues.title: flaky test: `TestInteropFaultProofs_VariedBlockTimes_FasterChainB/SuperRootInvalidIfUnsupportedByL1Data-fpp`
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
**CI run:** https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism/optimism/121281/workflows/bf0bc10c-07bf-4364-9756-aaeec46fcb0b/jobs/4703060/tests

**Date:** 2026-03-31

**Error:** Kona interop program exits 0 (valid) when the test expects exit 1 (invalid claim). Same root cause as ethereum-optimism/optimism#19828.

```
Error Trace: superfaultproofs.go:169
Error:       An error is expected but got nil.
             expected: *exec.ExitError
Test:        TestInteropFaultProofs_VariedBlockTimes_FasterChainB/SuperRootInvalidIfUnsupportedByL1Data-fpp
Messages:    expected kona interop program to fail, got: <nil>
             INFO interop_client: Successfully validated progressed transition state
             with commitment 0xf9e2f8d9...
```

**Root cause:** Same as ethereum-optimism/optimism#19828. When `endTimestamp` falls on a no-op boundary for the slower chain, kona correctly produces a valid no-op transition without needing L1 data. The test expects kona to reject `step1` because `l1HeadBefore` has no batch data, but since it's a no-op there's nothing to derive.

Encountered in the merge queue for ethereum-optimism/optimism#19814.

topIssues.title: flaky test: `TestInteropFaultProofs_VariedBlockTimes_FasterChainB/FirstChainReachesL1Head-fpp`
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
**CI run:** https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism/optimism/121281/workflows/bf0bc10c-07bf-4364-9756-aaeec46fcb0b/jobs/4703060/tests

**Date:** 2026-03-31

**Error:** Kona interop program exits 1 (invalid claim) when the test expects exit 0 (valid). Kona takes the no-op transition path and computes a valid optimistic block. The test expects `InvalidTransition` because `l1HeadBefore` has no batch data, but the no-op path correctly doesn't need L1 data — there's no block to derive.

```
Error Trace: superfaultproofs.go:165
Error:       Received unexpected error: exit status 1
Test:        TestInteropFaultProofs_VariedBlockTimes_FasterChainB/FirstChainReachesL1Head-fpp
Messages:    kona interop program failed:
             ERROR interop_client: Failed to validate progressed transition state.
             Expected post-state commitment: 0xffd7db0f..., actual: 0xf9e2f8d9...
```

**Root cause:** When a chain has block time > 1s (e.g. 2s), not every super root timestamp has a new block. Kona's `sub_transition` correctly takes a no-op short-circuit path when `safe_head.timestamp + block_time > agreed_pre_state.timestamp() + 1` — there's no new block to derive, so no L1 data is needed. The Go challenger provider returns `InvalidTransition` for this case when `RequiredL1 > l1Head`, but kona is correct: the no-op doesn't need L1 data.

The test's `nextTimestampAfterSafeHeads()` picks an `endTimestamp` that sometimes falls on a no-op boundary for the slower chain. When it does, the test's assumptions about what constitutes "insufficient L1 data" are wrong — the `FirstChainReachesL1Head` and `SuperRootInvalidIfUnsupportedByL1Data` subtests expect `InvalidTransition` but kona correctly produces a valid no-op transition.

**Fix:** `nextTimestampAfterSafeHeads()` needs to ensure `endTimestamp` aligns with a block timestamp for ALL chains, so every chain has a real (non-no-op) transition to validate. Alternatively, the L1-head-constrained subtests need to account for no-op transitions.

Encountered in the merge queue for ethereum-optimism/optimism#19814, rebased onto c865cf8108 (ethereum-optimism/optimism#19805).

topIssues.title: CI flake: contracts-bedrock-tests-upgrade proptest/fuzz failure with no diagnostic output
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
## Summary

The `contracts-bedrock-tests-upgrade` CI job can fail with a proptest/fuzz error that produces no useful diagnostic output — no failing test name, no counterexample details, and no JUnit test results.

## Example Failure

**Job:** [4593745](https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism/optimism/119645/workflows/0f6b41b7-6134-4d96-a2e6-d03ab88a8145/jobs/4593745)
**Variant:** `op-mainnet CUSTOM_GAS_TOKEN`
**Branch:** `aj/chore/migrate-op-reth-makefiles-to-just`

The entire "Run tests" step output (after go-ffi build) was:

```
Running upgrade tests at block 24659163
proptest: Saving this and future failures in cache/fuzz/failures
proptest: If this test was run on a CI system, you may wish to add the following line to your copy of the file. (You may need to create it.)
cc f67883e397bf6fee966e2318b3673f3fcdd4dde07fca11e86c955aafb79813cf
error: Recipe `prepare-upgrade-env` failed with exit code 1
error: Recipe `test-upgrade` failed with exit code 1
```

No test name, no assertion failure, no counterexample. The "Print failed test traces" rerun step (`-vvvv`) passed with **903 tests passed, 0 failed**, confirming it's a flake.

## Investigation Findings

### JUnit results are missing on this type of failure

CircleCI's `store_test_results` captured **0 test results** for the failing job, despite the JUnit pipeline working correctly for normal test failures (verified experimentally — see below).

### Forge writes valid JUnit on normal failures

We verified this experimentally: a deliberate `assert(false)` in a test file produced a complete 305KB JUnit XML with all 983 tests including the failure element. CircleCI captured all 983 test results. So the `store_test_results` pipeline and forge's `--junit` flag work correctly for standard test assertion failures.

### The proptest failure bypasses JUnit output somehow

The forge version in CI (`v1.2.3`, commit `a813a2ce`) uses proptest's `TestRunner::run()` for fuzz testing. Proptest has a built-in `catch_unwind` panic guard, so fuzz failures should be caught and returned as `TestError::Fail`. Forge handles this gracefully and creates a `SuiteResult` with the failure. The `test_collect()` → `test_iter()` → `test()` chain should always produce results.

Yet for this specific proptest failure, JUnit output was not written (or was written as invalid/empty XML). The exact mechanism is unknown — the file was not captured as an artifact at the time.

### The rerun doesn't overwrite JUnit

`JUNIT_TEST_PATH` is a step-scoped environment variable (set only for the "Run tests" step). The rerun step does not have it set, so `test-upgrade` takes the non-JUnit code path. The file is not overwritten.

### Mitigation: store_artifacts for JUnit results

PR #19581 adds a `store_artifacts` step for the `results/` directory (`when: always`) to both `contracts-bedrock-tests-heavy-fuzz` and `contracts-bedrock-tests-upgrade` jobs. Next time this happens, we can download the raw `results.xml` and determine if it's empty, truncated, or contains malformed XML.

## Reproducing

This is a non-deterministic fuzz flake. It was not reproducible on rerun in CI (same seed `42424242`, same single fuzz run). The proptest counterexample hash is `f67883e397bf6fee966e2318b3673f3fcdd4dde07fca11e86c955aafb79813cf` but without the test name, it's not actionable.

## Next Steps

1. **Merge #19581** to capture JUnit artifacts going forward
2. Wait for the next occurrence and inspect the raw `results.xml` artifact
3. If the file is empty: investigate whether forge's `std::process::exit(1)` in `ensure_ok` drops buffered stdout when redirected to a file
4. If the file has content but is malformed: file a foundry bug
5. Consider whether the CI should log the last N lines of forge stdout on failure as a fallback diagnostic

topIssues.title: flake: TestPreserveDatabaseOnCLResync, TestTruncateDatabaseOnELResync, TestCLUnsafeNotRewoundOnInvalidDuringELSync — stale engine RPC address after restart
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
## Flaky Tests

Three acceptance tests fail intermittently with the same root cause:

- `TestPreserveDatabaseOnCLResync` (`op-acceptance-tests/tests/safeheaddb_clsync`)
- `TestTruncateDatabaseOnELResync` (`op-acceptance-tests/tests/safeheaddb_elsync`)
- `TestCLUnsafeNotRewoundOnInvalidDuringELSync` (`op-acceptance-tests/tests/sync/elsync/gap_clp2p`)

## Error

All three fail with:
```
failed to init L2: failed to setup L2 execution-engine RPC client: operation failed permanently after 10 attempts: address unavailable (ws://127.0.0.1:XXXXX)
```

## CI Link

https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism/optimism/120052/workflows/55144005-177e-4fa8-b83e-0b782d8828e2/jobs/4629972/tests

Job: `memory-all-opn-op-geth` (4629972)

## Root Cause Analysis

All three tests follow the same pattern: stop L2EL (op-geth) + L2CL (op-node), then restart both. The issue is:

1. **Op-geth restarts on a new port** — `l2_el_opgeth.go` uses port `0` for engine RPC, so the OS assigns a fresh port each time. The TCP proxy upstream is correctly updated.
2. **Op-node reuses the stale config** — `singlechain_build.go:350` captures `l2EL.EngineRPC()` once at initialization. When op-node restarts in `l2_cl_opnode.go:68`, it reuses the same config with the old engine address.
3. **Op-node tries to dial the old port** — which no longer exists, fails after 10 retries.

### Why flaky, not consistent

The op-geth proxy address (`n.authRPC`) is set once and reused. If the proxy itself stays alive across the restart, the address remains valid. But when the proxy or geth is fully torn down and recreated, the downstream port changes while the op-node config doesn't update.

### Fix direction

In `l2_cl_opnode.go`, refresh the engine address from `l2EL.EngineRPC()` before creating a new op-node instance on restart, rather than reusing the stale config.

topPRs.title: supernode: Record full Output bytes with denied heads
topPRs.author: axelKingsley
topPRs.body:
# Tool Use Notice
Fully generated using repo and custom guidance. TDD.

Current Status: Author is self-reviewing.

The "DenyListOutput_Feature.md" file is a flight recording of the work the AI did and the direction I gave it.

# What
Replaces the recorded Denied Head (block hash) with a structure that includes Output

# Why 
Proofs needs to see both the pre-replacement and post-replacement outputs for every chain in order to correctly understand the roots being proposed and therefore correctly challenge games. We had been recording the block hashes, which allowed us to see that an optimistic root would differ from the validated one, but until now we haven't actually recorded these values.

# Related Work
This may not single-handedly address the SLA requests of superroot API for the Proofs team, but it's a known gap that factors into it.

## Summary
The superroot API needs the full `OutputV0` preimage (`StateRoot`, `MessagePasserStorageRoot`, `BlockHash`) to compute optimistic roots for invalidated blocks. Previously the DenyList only stored payload hashes, so this information was lost after engine rewind.
This PR changes the DenyList and the full invalidation data path to persist the marshaled `eth.Output` alongside each denied block entry. No backward compatibility is required — applications can rebuild their databases.
### Key changes
- **`DenyRecord`** gains an `Output []byte` field; `DenyList.Add()` accepts output; new `GetOutput()` query method
- **`ChainContainer` interface** updated: `InvalidateBlock` accepts `output []byte`; new `OutputV0AtBlockNumber` and `GetDeniedOutput` methods
- **New `InvalidHead` type** (embeds `eth.BlockID` + `Output []byte`) replaces bare `eth.BlockID` in `Result.InvalidHeads`
- **`PendingInvalidation`** carries `Output` through the WAL for crash-safe replay
- **`newInvalidHead` helper** on `Interop` constructs fully-formed `InvalidHead` with Output already attached at each creation site
- **Full propagation path**: `verify()` → `Result` → WAL → `applyPendingTransition` → `invalidateBlock` → `DenyList.Add`

### Propagation chain
verifyInteropMessages / verifyCycleMessages 
↓
 i.newInvalidHead() computes + marshals OutputV0 
↓
 populates Result.InvalidHeads buildPendingTransition() 
↓
 wraps Result in PendingTransition SetPendingTransition() [WAL write] 
↓
 JSON-serialized to bbolt applyPendingTransition() [WAL read] 
↓
 builds PendingInvalidation per invalid head (with Output) invalidateBlock() 
↓
 calls ChainContainer.InvalidateBlock DenyList.Add() [persisted to bbolt]

### Files changed (8 production, 8 test, 1 doc)
| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `chain_container/invalidation.go` | `DenyRecord.Output`, `Add(output)`, `GetOutput()`, remove legacy decode |
| `chain_container/chain_container.go` | Interface: `InvalidateBlock(output)`, `OutputV0AtBlockNumber`, `GetDeniedOutput` |
| `chain_container/super_authority.go` | `GetDeniedOutput` + `OutputV0AtBlockNumber` implementations |
| `activity/interop/types.go` | `InvalidHead` type, `Result.InvalidHeads` value type change |
| `activity/interop/verified_db.go` | `PendingInvalidation.Output` field |
| `activity/interop/interop.go` | `newInvalidHead` helper, `invalidateBlock(output)`, `applyPendingTransition` wiring |
| `activity/interop/algo.go` | All `InvalidHeads` assignments use `newInvalidHead` |
| `activity/interop/cycle.go` | Cycle participants use `newInvalidHead` |
## Tests
### DenyList storage (`invalidation_test.go`)
- All 12 existing `dl.Add()` calls updated for new `output []byte` param
- **`TestDenyList_GetOutput`** — 5 sub-tests:
  - returns stored output for denied block
  - returns nil for non-denied height
  - returns nil for non-denied hash at valid height
  - returns nil output when added with nil
  - handles multiple records at same height
- **`TestDenyList_OutputPersistence`** — verifies output survives close/reopen
- **`TestDenyList_GetDeniedRecords_IncludesOutput`** — Output field present in record list
### ChainContainer interface (`invalidation_test.go`)
- `TestInvalidateBlock` updated to pass marshaled `OutputV0` and assert it's stored via `dl.GetOutput`
- **`TestGetDeniedOutput`** — 3 sub-tests:
  - returns output after invalidation
  - returns nil for non-denied block
  - returns error when denylist uninitialized
### Interop types (`types_test.go`, `verified_db_test.go`)
- `TestResult_IsValid` — 4 sub-tests updated for `InvalidHead`
- `TestResult_ToVerifiedResult` — 2 sub-tests updated for `InvalidHead`
- **`TestInvalidHead_JSONRoundTrip`** — marshal/unmarshal with output
- **`TestInvalidHead_JSONRoundTrip_NilOutput`** — omitempty behavior
- **`TestPendingInvalidation_JSONRoundTrip`** — with output field
- `TestVerifiedDB_PendingTransition` — WAL round-trip with Output bytes
### Interop wiring (`interop_test.go`, `algo_test.go`, `decide_test.go`)
- `invalidateBlockCall` struct gains `output []byte`
- `mockChainContainer.InvalidateBlock` records output
- `mockChainContainer.OutputV0AtBlockNumber` + `GetDeniedOutput` stubs added
- All 15 `InvalidHeads` map constructions updated to `map[eth.ChainID]InvalidHead{...}`
- `result.InvalidHeads[chainID]` assertions updated to `.BlockID`
- `algoMockChain` updated with new method signatures + stubs
### Consumer mocks (`superroot_test.go`, `supernode_test.go`)
- Both `mockCC.InvalidateBlock` signatures updated
- `OutputV0AtBlockNumber` + `GetDeniedOutput` stubs added

topPRs.title: feat(op-reth): Drop interop transactions after reorg
topPRs.author: wwared
topPRs.body:
**Description**

This PR adds a wrapper type `OpPool` around reth's `Pool` type that allows overriding specific behaviors.

In particular, the code snippet that we're overriding here is the following: https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/blob/930f2a6eb257854138bb9e291c7013586fcd0223/crates/transaction-pool/src/maintain.rs#L412-L431

Inside `maintain_transaction_pool`, after handling a Reorg, the node reinjects the dropped transactions back into the transaction pool. When interop is enabled, this can lead to an infinite loop that prevents the chain from recovering, since if the dropped transactions are the interop transactions that caused the reorg in the first place, the node never recovers and keeps trying to re-add the invalid transactions back to a new block.

The problem: `pool.add_external_transactions` by itself does not allow us to know when a reorg has happened. For this we have `pool.on_canonical_state_change`, which tells us when a reorg has happened but not which transactions were dropped from the old chain.

Additionally, because `pool.add_external_transactions` is an async function, it's possible (even if extremely unlikely) that between the two function calls, some other task is scheduled to run and calls `pool.add_external_transactions` before the `maintain_transaction_pool` task can do it. If we only filtered once, this could lead to a scenario where the interop transactions don't get filtered after a reorg and lead to more reorgs.

This PR does the following:
1. When `pool.on_canonical_state_change` is called with a `PoolUpdateKind::Reorg` argument, we set a flag in the pool's state that a reorg has happened, and record the current time
2. Inside `pool.add_external_transactions`, if the flag is active, we filter out interop transactions (see `is_interop_tx`)
3. After filtering, clear the flag
4. If the flag was not set, but we're within `REORG_WINDOW` seconds since the last reorg happened, filter the transactions anyway

This ensures that:
- Even if the `pool.add_external_transactions` task ends up getting delayed and scheduled after `REORG_WINDOW` seconds, we will still filter it at least once: from the code, we **know** that there will be a call to it afterwards that we need to filter, at least
- If other tasks race the maintenance task and clear the flag, but then the task gets scheduled within `REORG_WINDOW`, the interop transactions being reinjected are filtered correctly anyway and we have no issues

The only remaining scenario where the filter wouldn't work is: a reorg happens, some other tokio task calls `add_external_transactions` without interop transactions to clear the filter flag, then `REORG_WINDOW` seconds pass before the original maintenance task calls `add_external_transactions`.

In this PR, I've set `REORG_WINDOW` to 30 seconds. This value is pretty high in comparison to the block times, and we could definitely set it much lower without much issues. I've chosen a higher value to be on the safe side.

Dropping the interop transactions like this is safe because the relayer can re-submit them after the reorg has settled.

The filter is enabled on op-reth startup by checking if interop is enabled in the chain config. This check is only done once, so a change from interop disabled to interop enabled is not handled by this PR.

**Tests**

Tests added to `pool.rs` and unskip `TestSupernodeInteropInvalidMessageReplacement` which now passes correctly with op-reth

**Additional context**

See also #19411

**Metadata**

- Fixes #19567
- Supersedes #19642 (this approach vendors the entire `maintain_transaction_pool` logic into op-reth to add the filter in-line, but this creates too much maintenance burden)

**Future work**

Ideally, reth's trait infrastructure would enable us to set an arbitrary transaction filter at different spots inside `maintain_task` so we could achieve this without potential race conditions and without needing to duplicate logic. Alternatively, we could modify some of the existing functions to pass more information to the pool functions so we could get rid of the `REORG_WINDOW` fallback.

Additionally, the existing `supervisor_client` filter located in op-reth's [`maintain_transaction_pool_interop`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/7c57cf9837850bc94625f73f5fee93cfcad58da2/rust/op-reth/crates/txpool/src/maintain.rs#L153) should probably be adapted to run via the `OpPool` type when `add_external_transactions`, `add_transaction`, `add_transactions`, `add_transactions_with_origins`, `add_transaction_and_subscribe` (etc) run instead. This would mean the pool can filter transactions out *before* they even get added to the pool in the first place.
